context: The Workdir page displays a registry table showing all prompts with their metadata and statuses. Currently, users can open a prompt's view modal in two ways: (1) by clicking the View button in the Actions column, or (2) by clicking on the prompt's title text in the Title column. Both actions trigger the same viewCompletedPrompt() function and open the same modal dialog showing the prompt's files (prompt.md, plan.md, questionnaire, implementation). This redundancy creates visual clutter and may confuse users about the difference between the two actions. The goal is to simplify the interface by removing one of these mechanisms while maintaining the full viewing functionality.

questions.question-text: Which mechanism should be removed from the Workdir registry table?

options.label: Remove the View button from the Actions column, keep the clickable title
options.pros: Cleaner table layout with one less column; More intuitive - clicking on the prompt title is a natural action; Consistent with common UI patterns (clickable names are standard); Saves horizontal space in the table; Reduces visual clutter
options.cons: View button is more explicit and discoverable for users unfamiliar with clickable titles; Some users may not realize the title is clickable without visual indication; May need to add hover styling to make clickability obvious

options.label: Remove the clickable title, keep the View button
options.pros: Explicit and discoverable - button clearly indicates available action; Consistent with action-oriented UI design; No ambiguity about what clicking will do; Better for users who prefer explicit buttons over clickable text
options.cons: Keeps extra Actions column; Less intuitive - requires scanning to the Actions column; Takes more horizontal space; Clicking the title would do nothing, which may frustrate users who expect it to be clickable

options.label: Keep both mechanisms but make them visually distinct with different actions
options.pros: Maximum flexibility for users; Could assign different behaviors (e.g., title opens in edit mode, button in view mode)
options.cons: Defeats the purpose of simplification; Adds complexity instead of reducing it; Would require implementing different behaviors for what are currently identical actions; Not aligned with the prompt's goal

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A is recommended because clickable titles are a standard UI pattern that users expect, especially in registry/list views. This approach simplifies the table by removing the Actions column (or reducing it if other actions are added later), creates a cleaner layout, and is more space-efficient. The title is the primary identifier for each prompt, making it the most natural clickable element. Modern web applications commonly use clickable names/titles in tables and lists, so this pattern aligns with user expectations. To ensure discoverability, hover styling can be added to make the clickability obvious.

questions.question-text: If removing the View button (Option A from Q1), should the Actions column be removed entirely or kept for potential future actions?

options.label: Remove the Actions column entirely for now
options.pros: Cleaner, more compact table; Reduces visual clutter; Simplifies the table structure; Can easily be added back if future actions are needed
options.cons: Would need to modify the table again if future actions are added; May require more significant changes later

options.label: Keep the Actions column header but leave cells empty
options.pros: Maintains table structure for future use; Easy to add new actions later; Signals to users that actions may be available in the future
options.cons: Empty column wastes horizontal space; Looks incomplete or broken; Not following good UI design principles (don't show unused UI elements)

options.label: Remove the column now, will add it back when needed
options.pros: Clean implementation following YAGNI principle (You Aren't Gonna Need It); Best user experience with current functionality; Easy to add back with future prompt if actions are needed
options.cons: Requires future code changes if actions are added; Minor development overhead when actions are introduced

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C follows the YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It) software development principle - don't add functionality until it's actually needed. Since there are currently no other actions planned for the Actions column, removing it entirely provides the cleanest user experience. The Workdir registry is meant to display information and provide quick access to view prompts; any future actions can be added through a new prompt when the need arises. This approach keeps the current implementation simple and focused on actual requirements rather than anticipated future needs.

questions.question-text: Should hover styling be added to the clickable title to improve discoverability?

options.label: Yes, add visual hover effects (underline, color change, or cursor change)
options.pros: Makes clickability immediately obvious; Improves user experience; Standard web UI pattern; Helps users discover the functionality without documentation
options.cons: Requires additional CSS styling; Minor increase in code complexity

options.label: No, the title link already has default link styling
options.pros: Simpler implementation; Link color and underline (if present) may already indicate clickability; Less code to maintain
options.cons: May not be immediately obvious to all users; Default link styling might not stand out in the table; Could reduce discoverability

options.label: Add cursor:pointer and subtle color change on hover, but no underline
options.pros: Clean look while maintaining discoverability; Cursor change is a universal indicator; Color change provides visual feedback; Avoids underline which can look cluttered in tables
options.cons: Requires custom CSS; Slightly more complex than relying on defaults

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C provides the best balance between clean aesthetics and discoverability. Changing the cursor to a pointer is a universal web convention that immediately signals clickability. Adding a subtle color change on hover provides visual feedback without cluttering the table with underlines. This approach is commonly used in modern web applications for clickable text in tables and lists, making it familiar to users while maintaining a professional appearance. The implementation is straightforward with minimal CSS and provides clear interactive feedback.
